A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] and $k, a > 0$.
Then:
:$\map \Pr {\size X \ge a} \le \dfrac {\expect {\size X^k} } {a^k}$

B_source.statement:
Let $Y$ be a non-negative [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] and $t > 0$.
Then:
:$\map \Pr {Y \ge t} \le \dfrac {\expect Y} t$

validity_conditions: For a > 0 and k > 0, x |-> x^k is increasing on nonnegatives, so {|X| >= a} = {|X|^k >= a^k}.
a^k > 0, so division is valid. (Chebyshev is the case k = 2 applied to X - E[X].)
proof_plan:
As $a, k > 0$ and $x \mapsto x^k$ is [[Definition:Strictly Increasing Real Function|strictly increasing]] on $\R_{\ge 0}$:
:$\set {\size X \ge a} = \set {\size X^k \ge a^k}$

By [[Markov's Inequality]] with $t = a^k$:
:$\map \Pr {Y \ge a^k} \le \dfrac {\expect Y} {a^k}$
